points.text: Buddhist temple cuisine, the vegetarian food eaten by monks, mostly served at temples.
Its philosophy avoids animal products and the pungent alliums known as gokun.
Temple lodgings (shukubo), where you can also join meditation and sutra-copying. It is a practical base for meals mainly if you stay there.
Temple cuisine traditionally avoids garlic and onion, but it can still use root vegetables. Jain travellers should ask when they book.
Show the waiter card from the scanner when you book, so the kitchen knows your diet.
